summary: 64-year-old man, 45 pack-years: 6 weeks of cough with blood-streaked sputum and 6 kg weight loss. NICE NG12: urgent chest X-ray / suspected lung cancer pathway.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Cough with haemoptysis and weight loss
inputs.hpi: Six weeks of cough, now productive, with streaks of blood in the sputum most mornings. Lost 6 kg without trying. Night sweats for two weeks. Hoarse for a month. Smokes 30 a day (45 pack-years). No fever.

exam.respiratory: Reduced air entry right upper zone. No wheeze.

inputs.socialHistory: Current smoker, 30/day, 45 pack-years. Retired construction worker.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected lung carcinoma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Haemoptysis with weight loss in a heavy smoker: suspected lung cancer. Urgent chest X-ray and suspected-cancer referral.

web.ccTemplate: Cough with haemoptysis and weight loss

mustRankTopK.note: Cough frame chips: haemoptysis, weight loss, night sweats, productive, >3 weeks (cough pool).

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: pane-engine models no lung cancer: with haemoptysis, weight loss and smoking it ranks pneumonia, oesophageal carcinoma and COPD. The SmartSymptomPicker ranking lists lung carcinoma (see dx-lung-cancer-top3-picker).

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Lung (1.1), upper GI (1.2), pancreatic (1.2.2), lower GI (1.3) and breast (1.4) cancer referral criteria
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (last updated 2023).

rationale: Permutation of the chronic cough case: the same cough frame with haemoptysis, weight loss, night sweats and smoking. NG12 1.1: refer people aged 40 and over with unexplained haemoptysis on the suspected lung cancer pathway.
